description: SLICE OF LIFE — after the Future Sound Systems OSC Recombination Engine: a scissor oscillator whose square slices two more oscillators, one gated on its positive half, one on its negative.

params.text: Sets the pitch of that section's oscillator in semitones, 54 either way from C4 at 261.63Hz.
Trims the pitch of that section's oscillator by up to three semitones either way.
Switches that oscillator's frequency modulation between linear and exponential; lit is exponential, where the modulation is added straight to the pitch.
Sets how far the frequency modulation input of that section bends its oscillator, 0 to 100%.
Sets how much of that wave goes into the section's mix. Below the centre the scissor gates it, silent at the far end; above the centre the gate is held open by that much and the wave is always heard.
Sets the pitch of the scissor oscillator in semitones, 54 either way from C4 at 261.63Hz; its square is what slices the other two.
Trims the pitch of the scissor oscillator by up to three semitones either way.
Sets how far its own frequency modulation input bends the scissor oscillator, 0 to 100%.
Sets the width of the scissor square, 1% to 99%, setting how much of each cycle goes to the positive section and how much to the negative.
Sets how far a voltage at the scissor pulse width input moves that width, 0 to 100%.
Sets how far the scissor pulse width bends the pitch of the other two oscillators, and does nothing while pulse width skew is off.
Steps through three settings for pulse width skew: unlit is off, then the positive oscillator falls in pitch as the pulse widens while the negative rises, then the two swap round.
When lit, adds the pitch reaching the scissor oscillator to the other two oscillators as well, so all three track one voltage.
When lit, hard syncs the other two oscillators to the scissor square and takes their own sync inputs out of use.
Opens the gate on both sections by a fixed amount, 0 to 100%, so they are heard even where the scissor square would shut them off.
Its value is read by the module and then never used for anything, so turning it changes nothing.
Sets how far a voltage at the VCA input moves that fixed gate opening, 0 to 100%.

inputs.text: Sets the pitch of that section's oscillator, tracking a volt per octave.
Bends the frequency of that section's oscillator, by the amount set for it.
A rising edge here restarts that section's oscillator, unless sync lock is engaged.
Adds to the level of that wave in the section's mix, 10% per volt.
Sets the pitch of the scissor oscillator, tracking a volt per octave.
Bends the frequency of the scissor oscillator, by the amount set for it.
Moves the width of the scissor square, scaled by the pulse width modulation knob.
A rising edge here restarts the scissor oscillator's cycle.
Moves the amount of pulse width skew, a fortieth of the full range per volt.
Moves the fixed gate opening on both sections, 40% per volt.

outputs.text: The sine of the positive oscillator with its lower half folded up, 0V to 5V, before any gating by the scissor.
The triangle of the positive oscillator with its lower half folded up, 0V to 5V, before any gating by the scissor.
The sawtooth of the positive oscillator shifted up to 0V to 5V, before any gating by the scissor.
The three waves of the positive oscillator at their set levels, gated by the positive half of the scissor square.
The sine of the negative oscillator with its upper half folded down, 0V to -5V, before any gating by the scissor.
The triangle of the negative oscillator with its upper half folded down, 0V to -5V, before any gating by the scissor.
The sawtooth of the negative oscillator shifted down to 0V to -5V, before any gating by the scissor.
The three waves of the negative oscillator at their set levels, gated by the negative half of the scissor square.
The triangle of the scissor oscillator, plus or minus 5V.
The sawtooth of the scissor oscillator, plus or minus 5V.
The square of the scissor oscillator, plus or minus 5V, at the width set for it.
The positive and negative section mixes summed together.
